task: Build a molecule-level literature dataset of experimental passive blood-brain barrier permeability evidence. Include PAMPA-BBB, brain endothelial cell permeability, MDCK or related passive permeability assays, transcellular Papp, membrane partitioning, and experimentally reported passive diffusion conclusions.
task_instantiation:
Extract molecule-level experimental evidence of passive blood-brain barrier (BBB) permeability. Create one record for each explicitly attributed molecule or explicitly named molecule class × distinct assay condition/result. Valid evidence is: (1) BBB-specific PAMPA; (2) another PAMPA result explicitly presented as BBB/CNS penetration evidence; (3) a brain endothelial/BBB cell model reporting transcellular permeability or Papp; (4) MDCK, MDCK-MDR1, Caco-2, or a related monolayer result explicitly used to assess passive/transcellular permeability relevant to BBB/CNS penetration; (5) membrane partitioning such as IAM-HPLC explicitly presented as relevant to passive BBB permeability; or (6) an explicit experimentally based statement that the entity crosses or fails to cross the BBB specifically by passive diffusion. Include assay controls when they have their own result. A molecule tested within an extract/mixture is valid only when the assay result is explicitly attributed to that molecule.

Exclude in vivo brain/plasma or CSF measurements, tissue detection, pharmacokinetics, ex vivo pharmacodynamic effects, behavioral/target-inhibition evidence, computational predictions, calculated/predicted logBB, transporter substrate or efflux-ratio evidence alone, formulations and delivery methods, generic passive permeability/cytotoxicity not tied to BBB/CNS, and conclusions based only on indirect in vivo or ex vivo effects. Also exclude assay-development observations about solvents or membrane materials, method recommendations, unstirred-layer thickness, cell-free blank inserts, and aggregate compound-set correlations/regressions. Generic PAMPA is out of scope unless the paper explicitly links that result to BBB/CNS. Do not create separate member records from a collective class claim; create one class record only if the class itself is available as an entity.

For each molecule and assay condition, make one record—not one per replicate and not one per metric. If one assay row reports multiple endpoints, store the principal permeability endpoint in `metric_name`/`metric_value`, prioritizing Pe, Papp, or Pm over a log endpoint, transport percentage, acceptor concentration, or partition coefficient; preserve secondary endpoints in `extra_details`. Separate records for genuinely distinct systems or conditions, including different permeability directions. Copy endpoint notation exactly: `logPe` and `-logPe` are different and the numeric sign must match the source. Copy units and multipliers exactly and never convert, normalize, or repair suspicious units.

Numeric values directly stated in prose or readable from tables/figures are valid. Qualitative-only results are valid only if the experiment explicitly attributes a BBB passive-permeability conclusion to the entity. Set `passive_bbb_interpretation` only from the author's explicit label or wording for that same entity/result: CNS+, penetrates/permeable, or high/acceptable/excellent permeability = `permeable_or_high`; CNS−, does not penetrate/impermeable, or low/limited permeability = `impermeable_or_low`; intermediate/moderate/borderline/uncertain = `intermediate_or_uncertain`; otherwise `not_stated`. A control called a “high-permeability control/standard” may receive `permeable_or_high` only when that designation explicitly applies to its result. Never derive a label from a numeric threshold, comparison, similarity to controls, assay convention, or outside knowledge. A merely comparative statement such as “more permeable than” without an absolute result or absolute author label is not a record. Do not add interpretive words absent from the source.

Choose `assay_type` strictly from the allowed values and spell it exactly. Use `PAMPA-BBB` whenever the source or established table/method context identifies the measurement as BBB-PAMPA/PAMPA-BBB, even if the immediate result sentence only says BBB permeability or logPe. Use `PAMPA_other` only for a non-BBB-named PAMPA explicitly linked to CNS/BBB. Use `experimental_passive_conclusion` only when the authors explicitly say “passive diffusion/passive permeation” across the BBB and no qualifying in-scope assay type is identifiable; never use it for indirect PK, tissue, ex vivo, behavioral, or pharmacodynamic evidence.

Use the top-level `global_identifier` for the exact tested molecule/class whenever available. Do not emit a record if the evidence cannot be unambiguously attributed to that entity; do not distribute a group statement to named members unless each member is explicitly assigned the result. Assume an intact barrier and routine assay conditions by default. Put only exceptional interpretation-changing conditions (disease/knockout model, transporter inhibition, deliberate barrier disruption, or molecule tested only within an extract) in `qualifying_conditions`; otherwise null. Put exact routine details in `biological_system` or `extra_details`. For directional cell data, copy only the literal direction notation and any direction name exactly as printed; never infer that A→B or B→A means absorptive, secretory, or eliminatory.

schema_spec.name: assay_type
schema_spec.description: Evidence category; select and spell exactly one allowed value. PAMPA-BBB includes BBB-PAMPA and PAMPA explicitly tailored to BBB.

schema_spec.name: biological_system
schema_spec.description: Exact named membrane, cell line/model, species source, or partitioning system (e.g., porcine brain lipid PAMPA, hCMEC/D3, MDCK-MDR1, IAM-HPLC); null if unstated.

schema_spec.name: metric_name
schema_spec.description: Exact notation/name of the primary measured endpoint, such as Pe, Papp, Pm, logPe, -logPe, transport percentage, or logK_IAM/W; null for qualitative-only evidence.

schema_spec.name: metric_value
schema_spec.description: Primary endpoint's numeric value at exactly the reported scale and sign, without conversion; null for qualitative-only evidence.

schema_spec.name: metric_uncertainty
schema_spec.description: Numeric uncertainty paired with the primary value at the same scale; null if absent. State SD/SEM/range type in extra_details.

schema_spec.name: metric_units
schema_spec.description: Units and multiplier exactly as reported; use null when absent. Do not infer unitless or repair a suspected error.

schema_spec.name: passive_bbb_interpretation
schema_spec.description: Author's explicit interpretation for this entity/result. Intermediate and moderate map to intermediate_or_uncertain. Use not_stated rather than inferring from a value, threshold, comparison, or control similarity.

schema_spec.name: qualifying_conditions
schema_spec.description: Exceptional conditions limiting generalization, such as barrier disruption, disease/knockout cells, transporter inhibition, or molecule tested only within an extract; null for routine/unspecified conditions.

schema_spec.name: extra_details
schema_spec.description: Free-form string for additional details that do not fit other top-level fields.
